source.title: Provable Generalization Bounds for Deep Neural Networks with Adaptive Regularization

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though its title metadata conflicts with the paper title in the text. The supplied version date is 3 Nov 2026, later than the stated current date.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a gradient-adaptive Gaussian dropout method changes held-out accuracy, using a different dropout method and accuracy comparison than the claim versions’ cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out mean-predictor accuracy for MAGDrop against deterministic baselines. Those results bear on V6. The Gibbs-risk and PAC-Bayes-bound results concern a different predictor and certification objective, so they are not rows for the stated versions. Cited prior results are not extracted as this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The convolutional-classifier experiments compare held-out accuracy with and without adaptive Gaussian dropout, bearing on V6 under a different dropout method. Certification and perturbation-sensitivity results do not test V7's relation between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: low-dimensional posterior structure dominates the certificate improvement, adaptive variance has no consistent advantage over random or shuffled controls, CIFAR-10 certification incurs a modest mean-predictor accuracy cost, and ImageNet results demonstrate compatibility with strong recipes. The certificates apply to Gibbs predictors, not the reported mean predictors.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces gradient-momentum-adapted Gaussian noise in a Bayesian classifier layer and a low-rank posterior for PAC-Bayes certification. It does not reproduce the fixed-rate dropout experiments described in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: The CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K accuracy comparisons differ by dataset, architecture, and training protocol. ImageNet results are single-run comparisons; CIFAR-10 CNN results are reported as seed summaries.

fits_no_version.finding: ViT-Base/16 reaches 78.57% versus 78.51% baseline best accuracy in single ImageNet runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive Gaussian dropout preserves transformer accuracy under a strong ImageNet training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Controlled PCA and random-QR comparisons link posterior-noise orientation to Gibbs risk and certificate quality; PCA mean predictors are more accurate at ranks up to 50 despite looser certificates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Posterior perturbation sensitivity and certificate quality can differ from mean-predictor accuracy.

record.problems: The ImageNet accuracy comparisons are single runs without stated uncertainty. The CIFAR-10 accuracy comparisons use different training and certification setups from the standard-dropout conditions in V6. For the CIFAR-10 CNN, the paper reports a three-seed mean and SD, but the ResNet-20 accuracy is stated without uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying held-out accuracy results left out. Gibbs-risk, KL, PAC-Bayes-bound, timing, and posterior-sensitivity results were omitted because they do not measure the held-out accuracy behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Network widening beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Standard activation dropout, fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive dropout, and removing dropout together with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking measured training–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Table VI reports 82.02% mean-predictor accuracy for fixed-variance subspace training versus 84.43% for the deterministic baseline and 82.00% for adaptive MAGDrop-Subspace. This missing control shows nearly identical accuracy with fixed and adaptive variance; the scope qualification also rests on this text-only result.
missing.locator: Section IV, cross-architecture certification; Table VI

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. No result establishes a dropout accuracy benefit within V6. The supplied version date, 3 November 2026, precedes the environment date, 14 November 2026; the record's future-date warning is incorrect.

versions.untested_parts: Standard fixed-rate dropout; fully connected and convolutional classifiers under the specific training-set-size regimes in the version; removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
